deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. Folio 36r is a scratch sheet with three unrelated layers. (A) Combinatorial notes on genus-3 theta characteristics. (B) A short linear-algebra computation with linear forms x, y, z, t, u and parameters α, β, γ, β^-1, γ^-1. (C) Numerical and physical notes in the right column (mm, 'gran', decimals). That column is written with the sheet turned 180°, so it reads upside down in the image.

CONTEXT. The previous page (35v) lists the 28 odd characteristics of genus 3 as pairs ij from {1..8}. It also lists Fano-type triples and quadruples (1346, 1357, ...) and three-term relations such as 13.46+14.36+16.34=0. The next page (36v) opens with the quartic √(x(αx+βy+γz)) + √(y(α'x+β'y+γ'z)) + √(z(α''x+β''y+γ''z)) = 0. This is Riemann's normal form of the plane quartic through its bitangents. 36v also has letter-sum calculus with characteristics written as sums of basic symbols n, p, q, r, ϑ, ε, f. It records parity statements ('gerade' = even, 'ungerade' = odd) and counts such as 28·27·16/(1·2·3) and 36·35·16/(1·2·3). This page belongs to the same work: Riemann's study of the case p = 3 (bitangents, Aronhold-type sets, characteristic relations).

(A) CHARACTERISTIC COMBINATORICS (upper left, upper right, lower left, bottom).
- Upper left. Lines headed p, q, s, r are each followed by strings of letter sums ending in words that are most plausibly 'gerade' or 'ungerade'. This is a parity table: for each basic symbol it records which of its sums with other symbols give even and which give odd characteristics.
- Upper right (faint). Similar entries: 'd e f ... gerade', 'p q r ... gerade ... ungerade', a column 'd+p, e+p, f+q', and the line 'p+q+r+d+e+f gerade'.
- Lower left. Two 3×3 arrays:
  d+p d+q d+r / e+p e+q e+r / f+p f+q f+r,
  then a permuted version d+p d+q / e+q e+p / f+q f+p.
  These are captioned with a word beginning 'Dreieck...' (triangles; Riemann's term for triples of characteristics, cf. azygetic triads).
- Also present: n+p n+q n+r / n+q+r n+p+r n+p+q. These are exactly the rows that open the systematic computation on 36v.
- Bottom. A list beginning with o (zero characteristic), then 'p+q+r', 'n+d+e+f', 'n+d+e+f+...', and paired columns d+p | d+q, e+q | e+r, f+q | f+p, again with 'Dreieck'-words.
- Interpretation (mine, plausible but not certain). In genus 3 the 64 characteristics form F_2^6. Choosing seven basic characteristics (cf. n, p, q, r, ϑ/d, ε/e, f on 36v), every characteristic is a sum of an even number of them, or the complement. The parity of a sum depends only on how many terms it has. That is the standard modern description via an 'Aronhold'/fundamental system (one convention: the 28 odd are the pairs; 35 sums of 4 plus 0 give the 36 even). Riemann is tabulating which sums are even or odd and grouping triples whose sum or parity behaviour makes them 'Dreiecke'. These are the triples entering the three-term theta relations of 35v and 36v.
- No derivation is carried out here; it is bookkeeping.

(B) LINEAR-FORM COMPUTATION (centre and left).
- Left column fragments: x+y+z; z̄+y+z̄; αz+βy+z/γ (or similar); αx+y/β+…; crossed-out lines; −1/α; (γ−α)u − 1/(α−γ).
- Centre:
  - 't − u − x + z − … = 0' (a linear relation among the forms).
  - 't − x − y, t + z + y, …' and '−(x+y)…, −u + z − x', 't + z − x' (trial combinations).
  - 'αx + y/β + γz = αx − γx + y(1/β − γ) + γu' together with 'u = x + y + z'. The transcription's '−γz' must be '−γx' for the identity to hold. It is then simply γu = γx + γy + γz.
  - A second line '= −(1/α ·… ) + … + y(1/β − γ) + (1/γ)u' does the analogous rewriting with reciprocal coefficients.
  - A further line expresses the result in terms of x, t, u with coefficients like (1/β − γ) and α(1−βγ).
- Lower centre:
  - [(α−γ)x + (1/β − γ)t]/(1 − γ/α) + y·α(1 − βγ)/(1 − αγ).
  - After a crossed-out line: (α−γ)x/(γ − 1/β) + t + y·α(…)/(1 − αγ), i.e. the same form renormalised so that t has coefficient 1.
- Purpose (my interpretation). This is the elimination needed to bring seven bitangents into Riemann's normal form. One takes x, y, z, the fourth line u = x+y+z, and further lines whose coefficients appear both as α and as 1/α. One then solves for the linear forms ξ, η, ζ in √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0. That is the equation written at the top of the next page. The coefficient pairs (α, 1/α), (β, 1/β), (γ, 1/γ) are characteristic of this normalisation.
- The computation is fragmentary and partly struck through. Only the first identity can be fully checked.

(C) NUMERICAL NOTES (right column, inverted).
- Measurements: '14 mm', '14 mm 5,1', '14 mm 7,6', '16 mm 1', '1 mm 55 gran', '60  3,5', '14 mm 17'.
- A division x/1800 with 440, 688, 0,43, 86 74 86.
- Decimal arithmetic:
  - 0,25527 − 0,10400 = 0,15127.
  - Column 0,15127, 0,010096, 0,002137, 0,04295, 0,20412, 0,16137, where 0,15127 + 0,010096 = 0,161366 ≈ 0,16137.
  - 32980 / 36222 / 0,69208 / 0,20797 / 0,0049206 / 203,22.
- These look like physical or experimental data (weights in grains, lengths in mm). They are unrelated to the mathematics.
errors: The identity αx + y/β + γz = αx − γz + y(1/β − γ) + γu, as transcribed, is false with u = x+y+z. It holds only with −γx in place of −γz. This is most likely a reading error, not Riemann's.

The lower fractions (normalising the coefficient of t) are too fragmentary to verify. The stated denominators 1 − γ/α versus 1 − αγ cannot be confirmed consistent without the missing relation defining t.

In the numerical column, 0,16137 + 0,04295 = 0,20432, not the 0,20412 written. Either a slip, a misreading, or a different operation is involved. 0,15127 + 0,010096 = 0,161366 is correctly rounded to 0,16137.

results.what: Parity bookkeeping of genus-3 theta characteristics written as sums of basic symbols (p, q, r, d, e, f, n), with 'gerade/ungerade' labels and 3×3 arrays of sums grouped into 'Dreiecke'
results.modern_name: Fundamental (Aronhold) systems of theta characteristics; parity of characteristic sums; azygetic triads in genus 3
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (p=3 fragment, publ. 1876 in Werke), Weber (1876), Frobenius (1880s); bitangent combinatorics also Hesse, Steiner, Aronhold (1850s-60s)

results.what: Rewriting linear forms of bitangents in terms of x, y, u=x+y+z, t, with coefficient pairs α, 1/α etc., aimed at the normal form √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0
results.modern_name: Riemann's normal form of a plane quartic via an Aronhold set of bitangents
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1864 fragment 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3', publ. posthumously); related work by Aronhold (1864)

results.what: Numerical and physical measurement notes (mm, grains, decimal subtractions)

deep.surprise_reason: Everything identifiable belongs to Riemann's known work on the case p=3: the quartic normal form via bitangents and the combinatorics of the 64 characteristics, which Weber published from Riemann's papers. The page is scratch work and bookkeeping toward that, with no new result visible.

checkable.asserts: αx + y/β + γz = (α−γ)x + (1/β−γ)y + γ(x+y+z), the corrected form of the central identity

checkable.sympy: a,b,g,x,y,z=symbols('alpha beta gamma x y z'); u=x+y+z; simplify((a*x+y/b+g*z)-(a*x-g*z+(1/b-g)*y+g*u))==0
checkable.asserts: The identity as literally transcribed (with −γz). This should return False, confirming the transcription slip.
Genus 3: 36 even and 28 odd characteristics. The odd ones correspond to pairs from 8 symbols (as on 35v); the even ones are 0 plus 35 four-element sums.
Values of the counting fractions written on the adjacent page 36v, which belongs to the same characteristic computation

transcription_corrections: Central identity: read 'αx − γx + y(1/β − γ) + γu' (not 'αx − γz …'), with u = x + y + z.

The right-hand numerical column is written upside down (sheet rotated 180°). Its true top-to-bottom order is the reverse of the transcription, e.g. 0,16137 / 0,20412 / 0,04295 / 0,002137 / 0,010096 / 0,15127.
The upper-left and upper-right letter strings are sums of characteristic symbols, each followed by 'gerade'/'ungerade' (even/odd), e.g. 'p+q+r+d+e+f gerade'. They are not unreadable words.

Lower-left block: also present is 'n+p n+q n+r / n+q+r n+p+r n+p+q' (transcribed on the page as x+p… but matching n+p… on 36v). The captions appear to be forms of 'Dreieck' (e.g. 'Dreieckspaare', 'Dreiecke').
Bottom line begins 'o' (zero characteristic), followed by 'p+q+r', 'n+d+e+f', 'n+d+e+f+…'.
